Summary Description: Dr. David Ebert is a multidisciplinary scholar whose work centers on visual analytics and data-driven decision support across health, information integrity, crisis response, and energy geoscience contexts. He contributes to the design and evaluation of visualization-centric infrastructures and AI-assisted analytics that enable rapid, trustworthy insights in dynamic, multi-stakeholder environments. His research emphasizes integrating visualization with emerging AI/ML techniques, collaborative platforms, and interoperable data ecosystems to advance preparedness, situational awareness, and evidence-based decision making in complex societal challenges.

Representative Publications.Title: Preparedness for visualization in the next pandemic
Representative Publications.Contributions: articulates a systemic view of visualization for pandemic preparedness, outlines infrastructure and workflow challenges (C1–C6), discusses platforms (CODEX, NUM RDP, FDPG), and promotes visualization as a first-class citizen in emergency response; highlights RampVis, ontological visual analytics framework, and DashSpace as foundational components.

Representative Publications.Title: TRUExT: Trustworthiness Regressor Unified Explainable Tool
Representative Publications.Contributions: proposes an explainable regression tool that integrates 13 communication-based NLP dimensions with a RoBERTa base to output a 0–100 trustworthiness score for news articles; demonstrates superiority of RoBERTa over BERT/DistilBERT across centralized and distributed settings; provides explainability factors for the score.

Representative Publications.Title: Development of Composite Clinical-Radiological Tool to Predict Functional Outcomes after Ischemic Stroke Treatment
Representative Publications.Contributions: develops a composite tool combining radiomic markers (CIV relative to AP/PA regions) with clinical features to predict discharge mRS; employs LOCO cross-validation with SVM, LR, RF, XGBoost, and feature engineering (FS1/FS2); demonstrates strong AUC performance and highlights potential for reducing inter-rater variability in AIS prognosis.

Representative Publications.Title: SMART 2.0: Social Media Analytics and Reporting Tool Applied to Misinformation Tracking
Representative Publications.Contributions: updates a real-time misinformation analytics platform with ML-driven misinfo detection, geo-spatial visualization, multilingual support, and human-in-the-loop feedback; demonstrates iterative accuracy improvements and case-study insights from the 2024 UK riots; emphasizes visualization-driven situational awareness and cross-platform data integration.

Representative Publications.Title: An image-based data-driven approach to estimate rock mechanical properties from SEM images
Representative Publications.Contributions: links SEM texture and pore geometry (notably pore aspect ratio) to Young’s modulus using regression models; compares feature sets with and without deep learning features; finds texture plus pore shape features best predict modulus, highlighting the limited added value of DL features given small sample sizes and dataset constraints.
